concept.name: Proof of stake
concept.definition: Proof of stake (PoS) is a Sybil-resistance and block-author-selection mechanism in which validators lock capital (stake) that can be destroyed (slashed) for dishonest behavior, and are pseudo-randomly selected to propose and attest to blocks.
concept.intuition: Instead of proving you burned electricity, you post a bond: misbehave and your bond is burned, so cheating costs you directly.
concept.mechanics: In Ethereum's PoS, a validator deposits 32 ETH, runs execution, consensus and validator clients, and is randomly selected to propose blocks in 12-second slots while committees attest each epoch. Casper-FFG finalizes checkpoints backed by ≥2/3 of staked ETH; equivocation or contradictory attestations are slashable.
concept.failure_modes: An attacker with >1/3 of stake can stall finality, and with a majority can steer the fork choice; long-range attacks and weak subjectivity require checkpoints; staking-pool centralization can concentrate effective control.
concept.misconceptions: PoS does not pay interest for 'locking money in a bank' — rewards pay for active validation duties, and downtime or misbehavior incurs penalties. Staked capital is not risk-free yield.
concept.example: A user deposits 32 ETH into the Ethereum deposit contract, joins the activation queue, and then attests every epoch (~6.4 minutes); if they propose two blocks in the same slot, part of their stake is slashed and they are ejected.
